note: The plain-language sentence is written for this game. The study is a real OSDR record on the same topic.

facts.text: Space radiation can damage the DNA inside cells. Scientists study how cells repair it, so crews can stay longer and stay safe.

study.title: Approaches for Surveying Cosmic Radiation Damage in Large Populations of Arabidopsis thaliana Seeds- an Antarctic Example

facts.text: With less gravity pulling on them, bones lose strength. Space station crews exercise about two hours a day to protect them.

study.title: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight [plasma proteomics]

facts.text: Muscles shrink in low gravity when they are not used. Studies on the space station look for ways to keep them strong.

study.title: Expression profiling of soleus muscle under the effect of simulated spaceflight

facts.text: Plants can grow in space. Astronauts have grown lettuce on the space station and eaten it.

study.title: Glycome profiling and immunohistochemistry uncover changes in cell walls of Arabidopsis thaliana roots during spaceflight: Advanced Plant EXperiment (APEX) 03-1 Raw Dataset

facts.text: Space has no normal day and night, so body clocks get confused. Good rest is part of mission safety.
Spaceflight can change how the immune system works. Staying rested and well fed helps a crew stay healthy.

study.title: Longitudinal transcriptomic and epigenetic analysis in astronauts reveals dynamic immune response to spaceflight [DNA methylation]

facts.text: Tiny microbes travel with every crew. Scientists keep track of which ones live on the space station.

study.title: Draft Genomes of Fungi Isolated from the International Space Station during the Microbial Tracking-2 Experiment

facts.text: Moon dust is sharp and sticky. Scientists study what it could do to lungs and machines.
